questions.stem: Set A is {ab, ba, aa} and set B is {ab, bb}. How many strings are in A ∪ B?
questions.explain: The union lists every string once: ab, ba, aa and bb. The shared string ab is counted only once, so there are 4.

questions.stem: Which set equals the complement of (A ∪ B)?
options: The complement of A, intersected with the complement of B
The complement of A, intersected with B
The complement of A, united with the complement of B
questions.explain: De Morgan's law for sets: outside of (A or B) means outside A and outside B, so the complements are intersected.

questions.stem: Which statement is equivalent to "if w is in L then the length of w is even"?
options: If w is in L, then the length of w is odd
If the length of w is even, then w is in L
If the length of w is odd, then w is not in L
If w is not in L, then the length of w is odd
questions.explain: The contrapositive "if not q then not p" is always equivalent to "if p then q". The other statements are the converse, the inverse and a contradiction.

questions.stem: Which string matches the regular expression `(ab)*`?
questions.explain: The star repeats the block ab zero or more times, so abab is ab twice. The others are not made of whole ab blocks.

questions.stem: A DFA has states q0 (start and accepting) and q1. Reading `a` switches between q0 and q1, and reading `b` keeps the state. Which string does it accept?
questions.explain: The DFA is in q0 after an even number of a's. The string aba has two a's, so it ends in q0, which is accepting.
